question.prompt: Camilla had twice as many blueberry jelly beans as cherry jelly beans. After eating \(10\) pieces of each kind, she now has three times as many blueberry jelly beans as cherry jelly beans. How many blueberry jelly beans did she originally have?

solutions.title: Translate the changing ratios
solutions.explanation:
The two ratios describe the counts before and after subtracting \(10\) from each kind. Let \(b\) and \(c\) be the original numbers of blueberry and cherry jelly beans. Then
\[
b=2c,\qquad b-10=3(c-10).
\]
Substitute \(b=2c\) into the second equation:
\[
\begin{aligned}
2c-10&=3c-30,\\
2c+20&=3c,\\
c&=20.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore \(b=2\cdot20=40\). After eating, she has \(30\) blueberry and \(10\) cherry jelly beans, as required. She originally had \(\boxed{40}\) blueberry jelly beans, choice \(\text{D}\).
